outcome: Decline in forced expiratory volume (FEV1) following pregnancy
Decline in body mass index (BMI) following pregnancy
cohort: The study included 249 women with cystic fibrosis who delivered 314 infants between 2001 and 2012, with a specific analysis focusing on 189 women having a first delivery.
finding: Pre-gestational diabetes in women with cystic fibrosis is associated with a significantly higher rate of cesarean section, but it does not appear to have a clinically significant impact on fetal growth, preterm delivery, or the changes in maternal pulmonary and nutritional status following pregnancy.
mod_finding: The rate of cesarean section was significantly higher in diabetic women (48%) compared to non-diabetic women (21.4%, p = 0.005).
followup_time: N/A (maternal outcomes assessed 'before and after pregnancy'; infant outcomes at birth)
cross-section timing: N/A (This is a retrospective cohort study, not a cross-sectional study; data was collected from 2001 to 2012)
birth_weight: N/A (Infant birthweight was an outcome measured, but no specific weight criteria were used for inclusion in the study)
